issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff’s readiness and willingness to perform a contract for specific performance must be assessed from the pleadings and evidence of ability and willingness to perform, rather than inferred from a delay in making up a court-fee deficiency.
material_facts: The plaintiff pleaded that he had always been ready and willing to perform the contract and was ready to pay the balance consideration.
The plaintiff deposited the balance consideration within the time allowed by the trial court.
The High Court treated the initial shortfall in court fee and the delay in making it good as evidence that the plaintiff lacked the capacity and willingness to perform.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff had established that he was ready and willing to perform his part of the contract; the court-fee shortfall and delay did not justify the contrary inference.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 requires a plaintiff seeking specific performance to plead and establish by evidence that he has always been ready and willing to perform his part of the contract. Failure to meet that requirement is fatal, but the evidence here, including the timely deposit of the balance consideration, established compliance.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding seeks specific performance of a contract.
predicates.plaintiff_pleaded_continuing_readiness: The plaintiff stated in the pleadings that they had always been ready and willing to perform their contractual obligations.
predicates.plaintiff_deposited_balance_within_allow: The plaintiff deposited the unpaid contract consideration within the time allowed by the court.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeking specific performance pleaded continuing readiness and deposited the balance within the time allowed, the plaintiff satisfies the readiness requirement.

issues.legal_issue: A court’s discretion to grant specific performance must be exercised on sound judicial principles, and a higher court may not reverse concurrent findings of readiness and willingness on an irrelevant consideration.
material_facts: The trial court granted specific performance, and the first appellate court affirmed the decree and the finding that the plaintiff was ready and willing to perform.
In a second appeal, the High Court reversed the concurrent findings and dismissed the suit, relying on the plaintiff’s initial court-fee shortfall and delay in making up the deficiency.
The Supreme Court found that the plaintiff’s ability to pay was demonstrated by the deposit of the balance consideration and that the High Court had relied on an irrelevant consideration.
issues.conclusion: The High Court improperly reversed the concurrent findings on an irrelevant ground, and the specific-performance decree was restored, subject to the further payment directed by the Supreme Court.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, the discretion to grant specific performance is not arbitrary; it must be sound, reasonable, and guided by judicial principles, and it is capable of correction on appeal. The High Court’s reliance on an irrelevant consideration and reversal of concurrent factual findings was manifestly illegal.

predicates.second_appeal_in_specific_performance_su: The proceeding is a second appeal in a suit seeking specific performance.
predicates.concurrent_findings_support_readiness: The trial court and first appellate court both found that the plaintiff was ready and willing to perform.
predicates.reversal_rests_on_irrelevant_considerati: The higher court reversed those concurrent findings based on a consideration that did not establish the plaintiff’s inability or unwillingness to perform.

issues.definition: In a second appeal in a specific-performance suit, when concurrent findings support readiness and the reversal rests on an irrelevant consideration, the decree should be restored.

issues.legal_issue: Specific-performance relief may be conditioned on further payment when the passage of time and appreciation in the property’s value warrant an adjustment that the plaintiff accepts.
material_facts: A substantial period had passed, and the value of the urban property had appreciated.
The court proposed that the plaintiff pay a further sum, and the plaintiff agreed.
The Supreme Court made specific performance conditional on depositing that further sum, in addition to the amount already deposited.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was entitled to specific performance upon depositing the further sum directed by the Court.
issues.legal_principle: In exercising its discretion concerning specific-performance relief, the Court may account for the passage of time and appreciation in the property’s value and condition relief on an additional payment accepted by the plaintiff. The judgment cites no earlier cases for this adjustment.

rule.if: specific_performance_appeal and substantial_time_has_passed and property_value_has_appreciated and plaintiff_accepted_additional_payment

predicates.specific_performance_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning relief in a specific-performance suit.
predicates.substantial_time_has_passed: A substantial period elapsed before the court determined the relief.
predicates.property_value_has_appreciated: The property increased in value during the elapsed period.
predicates.plaintiff_accepted_additional_payment: The plaintiff agreed to make a further payment proposed by the court.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance appeal, when substantial time has passed, the property has appreciated, and the plaintiff accepts further payment, specific performance is conditioned on that payment.
